description: cPanel API tokens of the selected account, available from cPanel 80: create a full-access token, list token metadata, rename and revoke. A created token's secret is returned once and is a credential; list never returns it. The client stores, refreshes, retries and revokes nothing on its own.

notes.text: The token reaches only the features the account itself has. The name may contain only letters, digits, dashes and underscores, at most 50 characters. Without expiresAt the token never expires; an expired token is not deleted and must be revoked explicitly. readonly: true restricts the token to operations classified read-only, with writes rejected by the server; it is independent of full feature access.

On cPanel 11.138.0.24 through both routes the result holds an integer create_time, the 32-character token secret and an undocumented whitelist_ips that was null. A name already in use is an API error. The server's handler rejects a nonzero expiresAt in the past, refuses team users, requires the account's apitokens feature and sends an API-token-created notification to the account's contact address when one is set.

The returned token is a credential and is shown only here. Keep the result out of logs. If this method raises PayloadMismatchException after an accepted outcome, the token may already exist and the exception's unvalidated payload may hold its only copy: handle that payload securely, do not retry, and revoke the token by name if it is not wanted. One invocation sends one form POST, with the name in the body.

evidence.note: Sanitized lifecycle probe on the designated test account npr through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge returned whitelist_ips null beside the pinned create_time and token. Cpanel/API/Tokens.pm on that server strips name, features, has_full_access, expires_at and readonly from the admin response but not whitelist_ips; the base class Cpanel::Security::Authn::APITokens::Object documents it as the allowed IP addresses or CIDR ranges, or undefined. The UAPI handler forwards no whitelist input, so only null was observed; the string item type follows that source description, not an observed populated value. The pinned pointer anchors the result object and does not document this field.

Pinned GET with x-readonly false and x-rollback none selects the default form POST. Required name (maxLength 50), optional integer expires_at and optional 0/1 readonly keep their pinned types; the result keeps optional create_time and token.

Sanitized lifecycle probe on the designated test account npr through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge with throwaway tokens, all revoked afterwards: form POST with name alone and with expires_at plus readonly=1 succeeded with integer create_time, a 32-character uppercase alphanumeric token and whitelist_ips null; a duplicate name returned status 0. Cpanel/API/Tokens.pm, Cpanel/Security/Authn/APITokens/Validate.pm and Cpanel/Admin/Modules/Cpanel/apitokens.pm were read on that server for the expiry rule, the team-user refusal, the apitokens feature requirement and the APIToken::Created notification. npr has no contact address, so no notification delivery was observed. The repeatable capture is tools/live-verify/tokens-section.php.

notes.text: Rows describe tokens and never contain a token secret. features is empty for a full-access token. expires_at null means the token does not expire. readonly is documented as present and 1 only for read-only tokens and otherwise absent or 0.

On cPanel 11.138.0.24 through both routes a set expires_at arrived as a digit string, not the pinned integer; it is returned as an integer. readonly was present on every row as 0 or 1. Every row also carried an undocumented whitelist_ips, null in each observation; the server's token class describes it as the allowed IP addresses or CIDR ranges, and this module offers no way to set it.

evidence.note: Sanitized lifecycle probe on the designated test account npr: a token created with expires_at listed that value as a JSON digit string through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge, while tokens without expiry listed JSON null and create_time stayed a JSON integer. The handler stores the request value as received. The pinned schema declares a nullable integer.

Sanitized lifecycle probe on the designated test account npr: every row, for the existing token and for throwaway tokens, carried whitelist_ips null through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge. Cpanel/API/Tokens.pm on that server returns each stored token object whole; the base class Cpanel::Security::Authn::APITokens::Object documents whitelist_ips as the allowed IP addresses or CIDR ranges, or undefined. Only null was observed; the string item type follows that source description. The pinned pointer anchors the row object and does not document this field.

Sanitized lifecycle probe on the designated test account npr through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge: GET returned rows with integer create_time, expires_at null or a digit string, an empty features list, integer has_full_access 1, name, integer readonly 0 or 1 and whitelist_ips null, with metadata.transformed 1. No row held a token secret. Cpanel/API/Tokens.pm was read on that server. The repeatable capture is tools/live-verify/tokens-section.php.

notes.text: newName follows the creation rule: only letters, digits, dashes and underscores, at most 50 characters.

On cPanel 11.138.0.24 through both routes a successful rename returned null, and the renamed token listed the same expiry and read-only flag. Renaming a token that does not exist, or to its current name, is an API error. The server's handler changes only the stored name, leaving the secret and creation time, and refuses a name that is already in use.
One invocation sends one form POST with no prior read. The token secret does not change, so clients holding it keep working; only references by name must follow the new name.

evidence.note: Sanitized lifecycle probe on the designated test account npr through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge with throwaway tokens: form POST rename returned status 1 with data null; a missing source name and an identical new name each returned status 0. The probe did not list between rename and revoke; the lifecycle captures of tools/live-verify/tokens-section.php do, and show the renamed row with the expiry and read-only flag it was created with. Read on that server, not observed on the wire: Cpanel/API/Tokens.pm sets no result data for rename and sends only name and new_name to the admin update, and Cpanel::Security::Authn::APITokens::Write::update_token changes the stored name in place, leaving the secret and create_time, and raises EntryAlreadyExists for a name already in use.

notes.text: The pinned text contradicts itself: the schema declares the 0/1 result as the function's data, while its description says the value is returned in the function's metadata, and it describes 1 as covering a token that does not exist.

On cPanel 11.138.0.24 through both routes the value is the function's data and the metadata is empty: 1 when a token with that name was removed, 0 when no token had that name. Both are successful calls; 0 is not an error and raises nothing.

Revocation is immediate and cannot be undone; a new token has a different secret. Revoking the token this client authenticates with ends its own access. One invocation sends one form POST with no prior read, so compare the returned value with 1 when removal must be confirmed.

evidence.note: The data schema is an integer enum 0/1 whose description states that 1 means the token was removed or does not exist, 0 means it was not removed, and that the system returns the data value in the function's metadata. The formal schema is kept as the typed result; the prose placement and meaning are recorded as contradicted by the server.

Sanitized lifecycle probe on the designated test account npr through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge with throwaway tokens: form POST revoke of an existing token returned status 1 with data integer 1 and an empty metadata; repeating it, and revoking a name that never existed, returned status 1 with data integer 0. Cpanel/API/Tokens.pm on that server passes the admin REVOKE result to result data, and Cpanel::Security::Authn::APITokens::Write::revoke_token returns 1 after deleting the named token and 0 otherwise. The repeatable capture is tools/live-verify/tokens-section.php.
